vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: baoyu-post-to-weibo
Version: 1.76.1

The skill bundle implements Weibo post automation using high-privilege operations including Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) for browser control, system-wide clipboard access via PowerShell/AppleScript (scripts/copy-to-clipboard.ts and scripts/paste-from-clipboard.ts), and automated process termination. A notable indicator is the instruction in SKILL.md for the agent to automatically kill Chrome instances (pkill/kill) without user intervention during troubleshooting. While these capabilities are aligned with the stated goal of bypassing anti-bot protections in complex web editors, the combination of broad system access and automated process management represents a significant risk profile.

llm.summary: The skill appears to do what it says (automating Weibo posts via a real Chrome session), but its runtime instructions and scripts require direct access to your Chrome user data, can kill Chrome processes automatically, and perform OS-level clipboard/paste automation — these behaviors are intrusive and warrant caution.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the supplied scripts: the repository includes weibo-post.ts, weibo-article.ts, Chrome CDP helper code, and Markdown-to-HTML tooling. Requiring bun or npx is consistent with how the scripts are executed. There are no unrelated cloud credentials or external services requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to locate and execute TypeScript scripts under the skill's scripts/ directory, read EXTEND.md preference files in multiple locations, and manage a local Chrome CDP session. Critically, the instructions explicitly say to automatically kill existing Chrome CDP instances (e.g. pkill -f "Chrome.*remote-debugging-port") and retry without asking the user. The scripts also perform OS-level clipboard operations and send real paste keystrokes to the frontmost application. These actions go beyond simple API calls and require intrusive system-level behavior (killing processes, activating apps, sending keystrokes).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only in the registry), but the skill bundles substantial code (scripts/ and vendored modules). Execution relies on local bun or npx-bun. No external download URLs or remote installers are used by the registry entry itself. Bundled code reduces remote-install risk but increases local execution surface that will run with the agent's privileges.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request API keys, but it reads and attempts to reuse existing Chrome user-data directories, DevToolsActivePort files, and may inspect process lists (ps) to find Chrome instances. Reusing a real Chrome profile means the browser's logged-in session/cookies could be used to publish on behalf of the user (which is needed for the stated purpose), but that is sensitive: the skill therefore requires access to your browser profile and the ability to start/kill processes and interact with the clipboard. These privileges are proportionate to automating a real browser session, but they are high-risk and should be explicitly accepted by the user.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request persistent platform privileges. It does read/writes temporary files and may reuse existing Chrome profiles, but it does not declare that it will modify other skills or system-wide agent settings. Note that agent autonomous invocation (disable-model-invocation: false) is the platform default; consider disabling autonomous use if you are uncomfortable with the script running without explicit confirmation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill implements a real-browser automation workflow and will execute local scripts that: (1) read EXTEND.md from project/home config paths, (2) inspect and reuse Chrome user-data directories (DevToolsActivePort), (3) may kill existing Chrome debug instances (pkill/ps usage), and (4) perform OS-level clipboard and paste keystrokes. These actions are consistent with automating Weibo via a real Chrome session but are intrusive and can affect your running browser session and private browser data. Before installing, consider: - Only use if you trust the source; inspect the bundled scripts yourself (they are included). - Run the skill with a dedicated Chrome profile (use --profile) or a disposable VM/container to avoid exposing your main browser session. - Be aware the skill will attempt to kill or start Chrome debug sessions automatically; back up important browser state. - If your platform allows, restrict autonomous invocation (so the agent cannot run it without your approval). - If you need lower privilege automation, prefer an API-based approach (requires official Weibo credentials) rather than controlling a real browser. If you want, I can point out the exact lines that perform process-killing, profile-file reads, and clipboard/paste operations so you can review them directly.
